newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR SURVIVES BEES AND MAD PLANE DASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR SURVIVES BEES AND MAD PLANE DASH.

text.p: Bruce Grobbelaar survived a swarm of bees, a furious onslaught from one of Africa's top strikers and a mad airport dash to keep a clean sheet for Zimbabwe in their draw with Ghana in an African Nations' Cup qualifying mtch on Sunday.
The group one game in Harare was one of 11 played in the qualifying competition at the weekend.
Grobbelaar, standing trial in Britain on charges of match-fixing, was granted permission by the judge at the crown court in Winchester to go to Harare for the vital clash.
The 39-year-old goalkeeper arrived on Saturday and flew back immediately after the match, dashing from the National stadium on the city outskirts to the airport to catch his plane.
In between, Grobbelaar made some vital late saves from Ghanaian captain Abedi Pele to salvage a draw after his Zimbabwean team mates had missed some good early chances.
The game had to be halted just before halftime, though, when a swarm of bees flew over the ground, forcing the players to crawl off the pitch with the shirts over their faces to avoid being stung.
The draw put Ghana firmly in the lead in the group.

Cameroon scored the biggest win at the weekend, beating Namibia 4-0 in their group five match in Yaounde on Sunday. Japanese-based striker Patrick Mboma scored two to take his tally to four in three games with Sporting Lisbon reserve Jean-Jacques Mise Misse getting the other two.
Mozambique got three goals against minmows Mauritius in Maputo on Sunday, scoring all in a seven minute spell in the second-half of their group seven tie.
Togo, Zaire and Zambia all won away from home to strengthen their chances of qualifying.
Togo went to the top of group six with a 2-1 away win over Liberia in the Ghanaian capital Accra on Sunday.

Liberia, playing at the neutral venue because of the conflict in their country, took the lead through Swiss-based striker Jonathan Sogbie but quickly lost their lead when Bachirou Salou equalised and then Assignon Komlaga got a second-half winner.
It was a second successive defeat for Liberia, who played without injured captain George Weah, in Accra.
Zaire beat Tanzania 2-1 in Dar-es-Salaam with the winning goal coming five minutes from time while Zambia retained leadership of group seven with a 2-0 win over neighbours Malawi on Saturday.

Ivory Coast, playing their first game under new coach Robert Nouirezet, beat Benin 1-0 in Bouake on Sunday with Guel Tchiressoa scoring a 12th-minute winner in group two. It was their first win since May last year.

Mali's game against Algeria was held up for 12 minutes while players and officials argued with the Senegalese referee after Mali scored in the second half. The goal from Bassala Toure came from a disputed free kick. The score remianed 1-0 and put Mali at the top of the group two standings.
In group four, the Central African Republic failed to arrive for their scheduled game against Sierra Leone in Freetown and have until Monday night before facing possible disqualification.

The Central African Republic played their first international match in almost 10 years when they started the Nations' Cup qualifying in October. Although there was no explanation on their non-arrival, the country has been suffering the uncertainty of an army mutiny over the past few months.

The qualifying programme was also hit last week by the defection of 16 Ethiopian players in Rome while on route to their group three match against Morocco in Casablanca, and the withdrawal from group one of Sudan.
